title: IAM Role Curation Engine and Upgrade Sanity Checks for Private Deploys
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Deliver a Terraform module and companion orchestration logic that curates least-privilege IAM role/permission sets for Private (VPC) deployments, validates upgrades via automated sanity checks, and provides continuous drift detection and human review flows before applying changes to customer environments.
goals: Provide opinionated, reusable Terraform role templates that map Redwood service surfaces to minimal permission sets
Introduce an automated pre-upgrade validator that runs policy tests and runtime smoke checks against a staging VPC before rolling changes to production/private customers
Detect and alert on IAM drift between the desired Terraform state and live IAM bindings with clear remediation guidance
Make the module easy to adopt: simple inputs, clear outputs (role names, policy ARNs), and example usage for common Private deployment topologies
scope: Author a new terraform module 'redwood/priv/roles-curation' that generates roles, role-attachments, and scoped policies
Implement a CI job (GitHub Actions) that runs the upgrade sanity workflow: terraform plan -> OPA/Rego checks -> apply to staging -> runtime smoke tests
Add a lightweight drift detector (periodic job) that compares live IAM bindings to Terraform plan and files an alert ticket with diffs
Produce docs and example stacks for 'single-account VPC' and 'multi-account with cross-account roles' patterns
out_of_scope: Replacing existing customer-specific IAM automation for on-prem private deployments
Implementing a full RBAC management UI in Console (we will link to Console rollout tickets separately)
Automated remediation that changes customer policies without explicit approval (alerts only in v1)
design_notes: Module inputs will favor explicitness: service_principals, resource_prefix, environment_tags, trust_boundaries
Policies will be authored as small, focused statements and composed into named policy modules (e.g., 'kv-cache-read-only', 'model-serving-exec')
Use Open Policy Agent (OPA) with Rego for pre-apply checks (policy library will include least-priv checks and deny-list conditions)
Staging smoke tests will include: assume-role check, basic API connectivity (list/describe), a guarded inference call against a canary model, and CloudWatch logs presence checks
Drift detector will capture both IAM role/policy content diffs and attachment differences; diffs will be stored as artifacts in the CI run and summarized in the alert ticket
implementation_plan: Week 1: Module skeleton, input/output schema, baseline policy primitives
Week 2: Implement role creation, policy attachment logic, and examples for single-account & cross-account
Week 3: Build GitHub Actions workflow for pre-upgrade validation with OPA integration
Week 4: Add staging smoke tests and wiring to the apply step (manual approval gate for prod applies)
Week 5: Implement drift detector and ticketing integration (create Linear tickets automatically on high-severity drift)
Week 6: Documentation, internal rollout, and 2 customer private deploy pilot integrations
rollout_and_migration_steps: Publish module to internal registry with semver and migration notes
Convert 2 internal Private deploy testbeds to use new module and exercise upgrade workflow
Run a dry-run migration against an early-adopter customer's Terraform state with their permission
Collect feedback, iterate on policy granularity and trust boundary inputs, then mark stable and announce to Solutions Engineering
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module passes unit tests (terraform validate + tflint + checkov) and example stacks can be applied to a sandbox VPC
Pre-upgrade CI workflow blocks applies when OPA Rego rules fail and surfaces human-readable reasons
Staging smoke tests catch at least one regression introduced by a model-serving permission change in an internal injection test
Drift detector runs periodically and opens actionable tickets with clear diffs; false positive rate is < 10% in initial pilot
Documentation and examples exist and Solutions Engineering has a runbook for migrating existing stacks
tests_and_health_checks: Unit: Rego rule unit tests for least-privilege assertions
Integration: GitHub Action run that does plan+opa+apply against ephemeral accounts
Runtime smoke: assume-role + simple inference API call + log forward check
Drift job: scheduled run that compares live IAM state to Terraform plan and produces a JSON diff artifact
Canary injection test: introduce a simulated permission regression in staging to ensure the sanity checks detect it
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly restrictive policies break customer installs. Mitigation: start with non-destructive staging applies and explicit manual approval for prod; provide an "escape hatch" input to grant broader permissions temporarily
Risk: Drift detector noisy on accounts with manual edits. Mitigation: include a suppression mechanism and classify drift severity; surface manual-edit audit info in ticket
Risk: Rego rules become stale as service surfaces evolve. Mitigation: attach rule ownership and add Rego rule coverage to the release checklist
Risk: CI apply to staging may be slow or expensive. Mitigation: limit staging applies to small resource sets and reuse ephemeral test accounts
